name: Angular
one_liner: Opinionated full framework — and a completely different product from AngularJS.
what_it_is: A comprehensive TypeScript-first application framework with dependency injection, routing, forms and HTTP built in. Recent versions added standalone components and signals-based reactivity, removing much of the ceremony it was once criticised for.
why_it_matters: The most common mistake here is conflating Angular with AngularJS, which is a separate and long-dead framework that still appears in this archive from 2017. Modern Angular is a serious choice for large organisations precisely because it decides things for you: structure, DI and conventions are prescribed, which reduces variance across big teams.
suitable_for: Large organisations that value enforced structure over per-team freedom
Teams that want routing, forms and HTTP without assembling them
not_suitable_for: Small projects, where the framework overhead dominates
Teams that want to opt out of its conventions
Anyone expecting AngularJS knowledge to transfer — it does not
